paper.title: Density Measures for Language Generation
paper.summary: Studies optimal index breadth through perfect towers and truth indices, and ordered-density guarantees for generated elements.

formalization_scope.summary: All six Section 2 results and six detailed main theorems have public Lean statements. Chronological rules satisfy the accuracy and density bounds. Under the unordered-sample definition in Section 2.1, Lean proves the tower and minimax results and gives counterexamples to the accuracy and element-density guarantees.
specializations: The indexed countable family may have duplicates. The public finite-history index rule works for every index naming the target. The historically reviewed selector theorem uses its first occurrence.
Chronological element rules take the finite list of observations through the current round. Ordered languages agree on the relative order of shared words as required in Section 5.
The set-driven results use a pure function of the distinct words seen so far. Both counterexamples hold even on injective exact texts.
The selectors use classical semantic access to the language family.
gaps: On exact presentations with repetitions, Claim 6.11 fails for the actual canonical run. The replay witness does not classify injective presentations.
The source-specific dynamic and charging arguments for Theorems 6.2 and 6.12 are not certified by the independent density proof.
Transfinite Cantor--Bendixson derivatives are not formalized; the current reusable topology infrastructure stops at finite natural-number rank.

claims.title: Index generation is valid in the limit and accurate infinitely often
claims.statement_summary: There is an algorithm that eventually outputs only indices naming sublanguages of the target and outputs an index naming the target itself at infinitely many time steps.

The chronological proof also repairs Definition 3.1 and the bound in Claim 3.2.

Duplicate languages are allowed; accuracy is language equality. The theorem does not require infinitude, and covers the paper's infinite-language model. Source-proof repairs, construction/proof correspondence, other results, and computation/density guarantees are not certified by this review.
